page.layout: Two printed blocks in reading order: first the running text of the page, a single column with marginal notes in the right margin; then below it a new heading "FLOS X." with its title, followed by a further running text column with marginal notes in the right margin. Printed page number "147" at top right; running head "FLOS IX." at top centre.

main_text.p: Ex his & similibus exemplis planum fit, legatorum παρρησίαν nonnunquam tolerari: sed mordaces & contumeliosas linguas semper & ubique coercere: ac proinde enixè cavendum esse legato, ne Principis, ad quem missus est, titulis aut juribus tam dicto quàm facto vel tantillum detrahat: sed eum potius observet & revereatur: imò & quantascunque ejus injurias non solum patienter, sed hilari quoque fronte perferat. Saepe namque accidit, ut potentior injuriam injuriâ cumulet: quam ubi patienter ferre videt: conscientiâ propriâ victus, beneficio eam obliterari desiderat. Probè hoc intellexit Franciscus Dandulus, Venetorum orator, in Galliam ad Clementem VII. Pontificem missus: ut eum, infestiorem Veneto nomini propter Ferrariam receptam, placaret: qui cum multa & varia secum agitasset consilia, neque à Pontifice iratiore quidquam impetraret: quadrupes effectus, catenâque ferreâ collum nexus, ad Pontificis prandentis pedes canis in morem sese substravit. Quo novo spectaculo Pontifex attonitus, illum in gratiam recepit: Venetoque nomini injuriam remisit. Egnatius lib. 6. c. 2.
main_text.head: FLOS X.
Legati magnanimi, ἀδωροι sunt & liberales.
main_text.p: CORINTHIORUM legati ad Dionysium Seniorem Syracusanorum tyrannum missi, cum ille pro more amplissima eis dona obtulisset, planè recusarunt: eò qp lex esset apud ipsos, ne legatione fungentes munera acciperent à Principe. Quibus Dionysius respondit: Rem profectò absurdam facitis, qui, quod unum bonum habet tyrannis, hoc tollitis: dum docetis etiam beneficium à tyrannis accipere periculosum esse. Adeo gravem judicabat Rex contumelam, oblata recusare munera: cùm hac unicâ re tyranni aliis se commendare possint: ut scribit Plutarchus in Apophthegmatis.

page.notes: The page has a catchword-like word at the foot ("Iohan") that is uncertain and may be a misreading; marked as doubtful. The marginal notes at the right are small and partly difficult to read; the reading of the note beside "Legatis" and the "Ioan. 4." footnote are uncertain. The Greek word "ἀδωροι" in the heading and "παρρησίαν" in the first paragraph are uncertain readings. The page number "147" and the year "1532" in the margin are as printed. The signature "Q 4" at the foot is uncertain.
